thread.title_full: WVU falls to Marshall in Sun Belt semifinal - NewsBreak

author: Cody Nespor
title: WVU falls to Marshall in Sun Belt semifinal - NewsBreak
text:
By Cody Nespor No media credit provided. ,
1 hours ago
MORGANTOWN, W.Va. — West Virginia was called for a handball in its own box with 36 seconds left in the second overtime period of its Sun Belt Conference tournament semifinal match with in-state rival Marshall Wednesday night at Dick Dlesk Soccer Stadium.
Marshall’s Joan Alves took the ensuing penalty kick and beat WVU keeper Marc Bonaire to give the Thundering Herd the 3-2 victory and book a trip to the Sun Belt title game.
“I think ultimately it’s just a really cruel moment in the game,” WVU coach Dan Stratford said. “We’ll have to lick our wounds and bounce back. We still have more football to play this season, that’s the good news.”
Watch: Dan Stratford reacts to loss to Marshall in SBC tournament The Mountaineers (12-4-3) held the advantage in the second half and into overtime and Stratford believed the game was destined to go to penalty kicks, as their quarterfinal game had, but the handball call in the final minute was able to give Marshall the win.
“The longer the second half went on, I thought the stronger we looked,” Stratford said. “The nature of when the goals came kind of brought the game to life. I was really proud of the effort and really proud of the performance.”
After an evenly-played first half, Marshall (11-2-5) struck first three minutes after halftime when Carl Romberg scored in the 48th minute.
West Virginia equalized five minutes later on a strike from Isaac Scheer that got past Marshall keeper Eddie DeMarco.
Marshall took a 2-1 lead in the 57th minute on a goal from Joao Roberto, but WVU equalized again 10 minutes later when Marcus Caldeira ripped a shot from outside the box past DeMarco. Calderia, the Sun Belt Player of the Year, has now scored six goals in his career against the Thundering Herd.
“With all respect, his worst miss of the year had come not long before that,” Stratford said. “Both the goals were well-taken, both strikes from a little bit further out, but it felt like the opportunity to equalize twice in a row helped gather momentum for us and put them on the back foot a little bit.”
Caldeira had an opportunity to score the first equalizer when he collected a DeMarco rebound, but his wide-open shot sailed over the net.
WVU outshot Marshall 11-5 in the second half and had a 5-2 advantage in corners. WVU did not, however, record a single shot in either the first or second 10-minute overtime periods. Neither had Marshall, until Alves’s penalty kick in the final minute.
Bonnaire made five saves in the losing effort. DeMarco also made five.
Next up for West Virginia is Monday’s NCAA Tournament selection show, where Stratford is confident the Mountaineers will get a better draw than when they were unseeded last year.
“Despite the outcome, hopefully (the fans) were excited and energized by what they saw and they’ll want to come out and support us in the tournament,” Stratford said. “We’re going to be playing at home again.”
Stratford said the team’s goals for the NCAA Tournament haven’t changed.
“We’re not trying to win a game in the NCAA Tournament, we’re trying to win the NCAA Tournament,” he said. “I still have absolute faith and belief that we’re still capable of that.”
Top-seeded Kentucky fell to UCF in the other Sun Belt semifinal on Wednesday, meaning Marshall will host the Knights in the SBC championship game Sunday at 1 p.m.
